hypotheses.claim: Under otherwise matched P01 conditions, substituting TEA for TEOA changes the CO/H2 distribution; if the difference disappears after strict matching and full controls, the original observation was condition-dependent rather than additive-specific. A discriminating prediction is that CO and H2 both change in a reproducible donor-dependent direction only when catalyst, ligand, absorber, medium, gas handling, and analysis are held fixed.
hypotheses.alternative: Apparent TEA/TEOA differences mainly reflect uncontrolled changes in medium composition, background photochemistry, donor consumption, or assay conditions rather than a real donor-identity effect on the Co-bpy catalytic manifold.
hypotheses.platform_and_comparator_choice: Primary test in P01 because it preserves the CoCl2+bpy, g-C3N4, MeCN/H2O, TEOA baseline closest to the researcher context; TEA is the single-variable comparator. P02 is supplementary only to check whether any donor trend survives in a cleaner homogeneous cobalt assay.
hypotheses.uncertainty: No supplied source gives a strict within-paper TEA-versus-TEOA head-to-head in the exact P01 recipe, so reproducibility and comparability must be confirmed before inferring mechanism. Background CO/H2 formation without catalyst is documented in related systems, which could compress or distort observed selectivity shifts.

candidates.title: Matched TEA/TEOA benchmark
candidates.purpose: Test whether changing the amine from TEOA to TEA alone alters CO/H2 distribution in the P01 Co-bpy/g-C3N4 platform under intentionally unmatched conditions to maximize donor contrast.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV059 and GX012 motivate a cobalt-containing photocatalytic CO2-reduction comparison using TEOA and TEA. EV063 suggests medium can matter, so the proposal transfers this by changing donor identity while also allowing donor-driven medium differences to remain, treating any resulting product shift as additive-specific. EV081, EV045, and EV022 support measuring CO and H2 together and including simple catalytic context controls.

groups.description: TEOA benchmark in the primary formulation family.

No-amine comparator to show the donor effect size against a minimal background.

comparisons.inference: Any CO/H2 difference is taken as direct evidence that donor identity controls selectivity, even if donor substitution also changes medium behavior.
Shows whether TEOA is catalytically active relative to no amine and provides context for the benchmark.
Shows whether TEA is catalytically active relative to no amine and provides context for the comparator.

procedure: Assemble the P01 TEOA formulation from the supplied system description and prepare TEA and no-amine variants by copying the same nominal setup.
Run illuminated CO2 photocatalysis for all groups in parallel reactors without additional matching adjustments so the donor environments remain naturally distinct.
Analyze headspace by the same GC workflow for CO and H2, preferably at one endpoint and one interim sample.
Compare product amounts and CO/H2 ratios across groups and rank donor effects by absolute difference.
measurements: GC-detected CO amount
GC-detected H2 amount
CO/H2 ratio or selectivity descriptor
Qualitative note of visible instability or precipitation after reaction
candidates.supports: A reproducible difference between E01G01 and E01G02 in either CO/H2 ratio or both product amounts supports H01 and is interpreted as mainly caused by amine identity.
candidates.refutes: Near-identical CO and H2 outcomes for E01G01 and E01G02 refute a meaningful donor effect in this platform.
candidates.inconclusive: Large run-to-run scatter, strong signals in E01G03, or obvious formulation instability make the comparison inconclusive.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the literature-grounded P01 TEOA formulation as the starting benchmark. If exact numeric settings are missing, select them by a short pilot that maximizes total gas production in the TEOA case, then copy the same nominal settings to TEA and no-amine without further correction.
candidates.limitations: This design wrongly treats donor substitution as a single-variable test even though amine identity can alter medium composition, proton behavior, and CO2 interactions. It does not isolate mechanism and weakly controls background artifacts.

candidates.title: Necessity controls and backgrounds
candidates.purpose: Check whether observed CO/H2 comes from the intended photocatalytic system and whether donor-specific backgrounds distort the TEA/TEOA comparison, using a compact control set.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV046, EV081, EV045, and GX008 support negative controls such as dark, Ar/no-CO2, and component omissions. The proposal transfers this logic to the P01 donor comparison and assumes that if the full system exceeds a small control set, remaining background pathways are negligible.

If CO falls under Ar in TEA, CO is attributed to CO2 and donor background is dismissed.
If gas production drops without cobalt in TEOA, the Co-containing formulation is treated as necessary.
The donor comparison is interpreted after the limited controls above establish acceptable assay validity.

procedure: Prepare the full TEOA and TEA systems plus one dark, one Ar, and one no-cobalt control.
Run all groups with the same reactor format and analyze CO and H2 by the same GC method.
Compare control outputs to their corresponding full system and then compare the two full systems.
If controls are lower than the full systems, proceed to interpret the TEA/TEOA difference as intrinsic.

candidates.refutes: Controls close to the full systems refute the benchmark and imply donor comparison is not meaningful.
candidates.inconclusive: Mixed outcomes across controls or large donor-specific background signals make donor conclusions inconclusive.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the same nominal settings as E01. If a control gives no detectable gas, no further optimization is needed. If all groups are near detection limits, increase irradiation time by pilot equally for every group until at least one full system exceeds blank noise.
candidates.limitations: Controls are incomplete because they do not cover all omissions for both amines, yet the design still treats them as sufficient. Multi-factor contrasts are present across some groups, but the card interprets them as decisive artifact checks anyway.

candidates.title: Donor amount series
candidates.purpose: Test whether any TEA/TEOA difference persists across donor loadings by sweeping donor amount and reading selectivity trends, assuming amount and identity can be merged into one practical causal factor.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV061 links TEOA proportion to CO2-reduction output and suggests donor concentration can alter performance. EV063 indicates medium composition affects CO/H2 in a CoCl2/bpy-related system. EV059 motivates applying such amount variation within the P01 TEOA/TEA comparison and interpreting the combined landscape as donor behavior.

Shows how TEA amount changes CO and H2 within one donor identity.

procedure: Choose two donor loadings spanning a visible performance range by brief pilot in the TEOA system, then reuse the same nominal low and high levels for TEA.
Run the four illuminated CO2 photocatalysis groups with all other nominal settings unchanged.
Measure CO and H2 by the same GC workflow and compare both within-donor amount trends and cross-donor differences at each amount.
Use the resulting pattern to decide whether donor identity or donor amount is the stronger determinant.
measurements: GC-detected CO amount
GC-detected H2 amount
CO/H2 ratio across the four groups
Simple trend direction with donor amount
candidates.supports: If TEA and TEOA remain separated at both low and high donor amounts, H01 is supported and the donor effect is treated as intrinsic rather than condition-dependent.
candidates.refutes: If changing donor amount dominates while TEA and TEOA overlap at one or both levels, H01 is refuted.
candidates.inconclusive: Crossing trends, strong instability, or poor signal at one loading make the identity conclusion inconclusive.
candidates.parameter_selection: Define low and high donor amounts by a short pilot that finds one underperforming and one stronger TEOA condition. Apply the same nominal low and high amounts to TEA without compensating for compositional differences, because identical nominal addition is assumed to create the fairest comparison.
candidates.limitations: This combines donor identity and medium perturbation issues and overinterprets nominally matched additions as chemically matched conditions. Two-point amount sampling can miss nonmonotonic behavior and cannot isolate mechanism.

candidates.title: TEA versus TEOA donor-side quenching comparison in the P01 baseline matrix
candidates.purpose: Test whether replacing TEOA with TEA changes upstream photoredox observables under otherwise matched P01-like formulations, providing a covariate for any donor-dependent CO/H2 shift without claiming full mechanism.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV053 and EV065 support transferable fluorescence/UV-vis quenching logic in donor-containing photocatalytic cobalt systems; GX007 shows TEA-for-TEOA substitution can change photochemical behavior; EV011 supports that TEA and TEOA form different donor-derived radical species after quenching. Proposed transfer: adapt these observables to the matched P01 absorber-containing formulation, with cobalt-containing and cobalt-free references to separate donor-side from cobalt-side effects.

P01-like absorber-containing comparator with TEA and cobalt components
Baseline donor matrix without cobalt components
Comparator donor matrix without cobalt components

comparisons.inference: Single-factor donor comparison in the full matrix. A reproducible difference in quenching observable supports donor-dependent upstream photoredox behavior under matched conditions.
Single-factor donor comparison without cobalt components. Similar donor ordering here would suggest an absorber/donor effect that does not require cobalt.
Tests whether cobalt presence changes the quenching response in the TEOA matrix; helps assign whether the measured signal includes cobalt-associated pathways.
Tests whether cobalt presence changes the quenching response in the TEA matrix; donor dependence of this cobalt effect may indicate altered interaction with the cobalt-containing manifold.

procedure: Prepare matched absorber-containing samples using the P01 baseline composition logic, changing only donor identity or cobalt-component presence across groups.
Record fluorescence and/or UV-vis responses under identical optical settings, including blanks for solvent and absorber-free backgrounds if needed for subtraction.
Run a small pilot to set sample absorbance within the instrument-linear range and to confirm that donor addition does not saturate or fully extinguish the signal before useful comparison.

Compare donor-dependent quenching trends first in cobalt-free matrices, then in cobalt-containing matrices, and retain raw spectra and corrected Stern-Volmer-style summaries only if linearity is empirically adequate.
measurements: Steady-state fluorescence intensity or lifetime proxy of the absorber-containing sample under matched excitation
UV-vis spectral changes during donor addition or short irradiation exposure
Apparent quenching trend versus donor condition in cobalt-free and cobalt-containing matrices
Background absorbance/scattering from donor, solvent, g-C3N4, and cobalt-containing mixtures
candidates.supports: A reproducible TEA-versus-TEOA difference in quenching observable under otherwise matched conditions, especially if the direction is consistent across repeats and not explained by simple optical background, supports H01 secondary explanation that donor identity changes upstream photoredox entry. If this covaries with later CO/H2 differences from the benchmark, it strengthens but does not prove a donor-photophysics contribution.
candidates.refutes: If TEA and TEOA give indistinguishable quenching behavior within calibrated detection limits in both cobalt-free and cobalt-containing matrices, a large donor-specific upstream quenching difference is disfavored as the main explanation for any product shift, though downstream proton or cobalt-state effects remain possible.
candidates.inconclusive: Strong scattering, overlapping absorbance, unstable baselines, or donor-dependent sample degradation that prevents reliable assignment makes the result inconclusive. A difference in quenching alone also cannot establish the active catalytic pathway or predict CO/H2 direction without catalytic correlation.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the same nominal absorber, solvent matrix, and cobalt-component presence as the verified P01 baseline. Because no exact optical recipe is supplied, pilot donor additions should set a range that changes signal measurably without complete quench or severe inner-filter artifacts. Accept Stern-Volmer treatment only over the empirically linear region; otherwise report descriptive matched-point comparisons.
candidates.limitations: This is a characterization proposal, not a catalytic readout. Signals may reflect absorber/donor or absorber/cobalt interactions without identifying the turnover-relevant species. In a heterogeneous g-C3N4 matrix, scattering and adsorption can confound fluorescence or UV-vis comparisons. Transfer from EV053, EV065, and GX007 is methodological, not proof that the same quenching route controls P01 selectivity.

candidates.title: Near-operando cobalt-state comparison under TEOA and TEA
candidates.purpose: Assess whether TEA and TEOA correlate with different cobalt oxidation or coordination signatures in the P01 primary system, narrowing whether donor identity changes the cobalt-containing catalytic manifold rather than only bulk assay conditions.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV059 anchors the CoCl2 plus bpy plus g-C3N4 plus TEOA formulation family closest to the target context. GX008 supports UV-vis, XAS, IR, Raman, and related operando-capable methods for homogeneous or mixed photocatalytic systems, while EV046 supports before/after and control logic but warns that recovered-state data alone are insufficient. Proposed transfer: use the P01 baseline and TEA comparator with matched catalyst-containing and catalyst-free references, prioritizing near-operando measurements over post-reaction-only inference.

comparisons.inference: Within TEOA, descriptive comparison for cobalt-state evolution under illumination. This is not a single-factor causal test because timing changes with illumination state, but it can reveal whether cobalt-associated signatures emerge or decay during operation.
Within TEA, descriptive comparison for cobalt-state evolution under illumination. Compare direction and magnitude with the TEOA pair, but retain the same descriptive limit.
Single-factor donor comparison before illumination. Any initial difference suggests donor-dependent pre-equilibrium or coordination differences before turnover begins.
Single-factor donor comparison at the matched illuminated state. A reproducible donor-dependent cobalt signature supports donor-linked changes in the cobalt manifold under operating conditions.

procedure: Select one primary spectroscopic mode with cobalt sensitivity available in-house or through a facility, and pair it with one simpler cross-check if possible.

Collect reference spectra for the full matrix and cobalt-free background, then acquire matched pre-illumination and illuminated-state spectra for TEOA and TEA formulations using the same sampling geometry and timing logic.
Use a pilot illumination window short enough to preserve measurable cobalt signal while still producing a state change, and freeze timing/handling before the donor comparison.
Interpret only features that differ reproducibly from cobalt-free backgrounds and that persist across at least one independent physical readout or repeat set.
measurements: Cobalt-sensitive spectral signatures consistent with oxidation-state or coordination-environment change
Difference spectra between pre-illumination and illuminated states under each donor
Background spectra from donor-containing cobalt-free matrix
If available, concurrent UV-vis changes of the full sample to track gross decomposition or aggregation
candidates.supports: A reproducible donor-dependent cobalt-associated spectral difference under matched illuminated conditions, especially when absent or smaller before illumination, supports a link between donor identity and the cobalt-containing catalytic manifold. Correlation with catalytic CO/H2 changes would strengthen this interpretation.
candidates.refutes: If TEA and TEOA give no reproducible difference in cobalt-associated signatures before or during illumination within the method's resolution, a large donor-specific cobalt-state change is disfavored as the dominant explanation for product differences, though subtle states below detection or non-cobalt factors may remain.
candidates.inconclusive: Recovered-sample-only differences, unresolved overlapping features, or spectral changes equally present in cobalt-free backgrounds are inconclusive for cobalt-state assignment. Even a clear donor-dependent cobalt signal cannot by itself prove the active species, rate-limiting step, or causal path to CO versus H2.
candidates.parameter_selection: Because no exact operando settings are supplied, choose the method by availability and cobalt detectability: low-barrier UV-vis if features are visible, or specialist XAS/IR/Raman if needed. Use pilot scans to determine concentration/pathlength or collection time that gives unsaturated, reproducible spectra and a short illumination interval that changes signal without complete decomposition. Hold reactor, gas handling, and optical flux constant across donors.
candidates.limitations: In situ active-state identity for P01 is unresolved. Heterogeneous support and mixed solution/solid phases can blur cobalt assignments. Pre/post contrasts are inherently time-coupled and therefore descriptive rather than isolated causal tests. This card characterizes state correlation, not full mechanism.

candidates.title: 13CO2 origin check for CO under matched TEOA and TEA conditions
candidates.purpose: Determine whether CO detected in the matched donor comparison is CO2-derived under both donor identities, protecting the TEA/TEOA selectivity comparison against donor-specific carbon artifacts or background CO formation.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV021 shows TEOA can participate non-innocently yet isotope labeling can still verify CO2 origin; EV046, EV022, EV082, and GX008 support transferable use of negative controls and 13CO2 plus GC-MS in photocatalytic CO2 reduction studies. Proposed transfer: apply reproducible 13CO2 labeling to the P01 matched benchmark for both donors, alongside key benchmark negatives, and interpret origin separately from selectivity or mechanism.

Single-factor isotopic-origin check for the TEA case. This tests whether CO under TEA is likewise CO2-derived rather than donor-specific carbon artifact.

Multi-factor contrast against a key negative control. Useful to bound catalyst dependence of labeled CO detection, but confounded by donor choice if only one negative-control donor is run.

procedure: Reproduce the matched P01 benchmark for TEOA and TEA using the same reactor, gas handling, illumination, and sampling workflow as the benchmark experiment, substituting labeled CO2 only where specified.
Run GC-MS with unlabeled and labeled CO references or established mass-fragment checks to verify that the instrument can distinguish labeled from unlabeled CO under the expected small-signal regime.
Include at least one labeled-gas negative control omitting cobalt components, and retain benchmark dark or no-CO2 controls from the parent assay if available in the same campaign.
Interpret isotopic origin separately from total CO/H2 performance: first ask whether CO is CO2-derived in each donor case, then compare donor-dependent CO amount only within the labeled matched pair.
measurements: GC-MS isotopic pattern for CO under 13CO2 and under unlabeled CO2 references
CO and H2 amounts from the same matched runs to preserve the donor comparison context
Blank and negative-control signals for reactor or analytical background CO
If measurable, reproducibility of labeled CO detection across repeat injections or runs
candidates.supports: Detection of the labeled CO signature in both donor conditions, with the corresponding unlabeled reference pattern in the natural-abundance runs and little or no labeled CO in the negative control, supports the claim that observed CO in the donor comparison is genuinely CO2-derived. This validates interpreting donor-dependent CO changes as altered CO2-reduction output rather than obvious carbon-source artifact.
candidates.refutes: If CO detected in a donor condition lacks the expected labeled signature under 13CO2, or if similar labeled CO appears in the key negative control, the central TEA/TEOA CO comparison is undermined and donor-specific or assay-background artifacts become a stronger explanation.
candidates.inconclusive: Very low CO signal, overlapping mass fragments, memory effects, or inconsistent gas handling can make origin assignment inconclusive. Even a positive 13CO2 result does not explain why TEA and TEOA differ; it only bounds the carbon-source question.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the same matched formulation and illumination program as the verified benchmark. Because no isotope-analysis recipe is supplied, first calibrate GC-MS retention and fragment assignment with unlabeled and labeled CO standards or validated instrument checks, then choose a sampling volume and run time that detect the smallest benchmark CO signal without overload. If product is near detection limit, prioritize fewer well-controlled labeled runs over a broad matrix.
candidates.limitations: This card verifies product origin, not mechanism. A positive result cannot distinguish donor-photophysics, proton management, medium effects, or cobalt-state explanations. The negative control is not a perfectly matched single-factor test if only one donor identity is used there; conclusions from that contrast must stay bounded.

evidence.claim: Literature reports a g-C3N4-assisted molecular CO2 photoreduction formulation using CoCl2 plus bipyridine to form Co(bpy)3Cl2 in MeCN/H2O with TEOA, and the table explicitly lists alternative amines including triethylamine with different CO/H2 selectivities under related conditions.
evidence.transfer_limit: The exact active cobalt species may depend on in situ assembly and support effects from g-C3N4 or Co-ZIF-9; the snippet does not provide a direct TEA-versus-TEOA head-to-head in one unchanged formulation, so transfer to the researcher's specific Co(II)-bipyridine system requires verification.
evidence.reason: This is the closest direct match to the target topic because it explicitly combines cobalt chloride and bipyridine in a CO2 photocatalytic system and mentions TEOA while tabulating triethylamine and other amines as donor variants affecting CO/H2 selectivity. It supports selecting this formulation family for controlled TEA/TEOA comparison, while preserving uncertainty about species identity and exact comparability.

evidence.reason: Relevant because it explicitly uses CoCl2 and bipyridine in photocatalytic CO2 reduction with CO/H2 as outputs and demonstrates that product distribution is sensitive to medium composition. This strengthens the need for strict comparability controls when testing TEA versus TEOA in related systems.

evidence.transfer_limit: This is general methods guidance rather than a specific Co(II)-bipyridine/TEA/TEOA experiment. Applicability depends on the actual formulation, concentrations, and detectable intermediates.
evidence.reason: Included because it directly supports rigorous experimental design and characterization choices for the target comparison, especially origin controls and suitable spectroscopies for homogeneous photocatalytic CO2 reduction.

evidence.role: direct donor-substitution evidence affecting photochemical behavior
evidence.claim: In a photocatalytic system, TEA was used to replace TEOA, and upon irradiation the Acr+TEA solution formed leuco-Acr within 10 min, but the rate of Acr fading was lower than with TEOA, indicating different reductive quenching behavior of the electron donor.
evidence.transfer_limit: This is an H2-production system with Acr photosensitizer and cobalt oxide in DMF/H2O, not CO2 reduction with a Co(II)-bipyridine molecular catalyst. It informs donor effects on photoredox and stability, not product selectivity in the target system.
evidence.reason: Included because it directly compares TEA and TEOA under irradiation and reports a measurable kinetic difference, supporting the hypothesis that donor identity can alter upstream photochemical steps even when the catalytic platform differs.
